## Today's Agenda

- Install four programs: R, VS Code, Quarto, and Git
- Prove all four are really there
- Make your own copy of the course workspace and bring it to your laptop
- Run the setup check file and read what it says
- What to do when something breaks

## What This Video Is For

- We do one thing: get four programs onto your laptop, make your own copy of the course workspace, and run a file that proves it all works
- **Work along with me.** Do not watch first and do it later
- Pause whenever you need to, and rewind anything that goes past too fast
- Nothing here is a race, and the video will wait

## What You Will Have at the End

- R, VS Code, Quarto, and Git installed and answering
- Your own repository on GitHub, named `mc451-workspace`
- That folder open in VS Code on your laptop
- A setup check that runs and comes back green

**Project Setup**, 25 points, is due Friday, September 11, 11:59 PM.

## Something Is Going to Break

- Setup breaks in every section, every semester, for somebody
- It is never because that person is bad at this
- It is one version number disagreeing with another
- **Pause the video the moment something looks wrong.** Do not push on and hope
- Fifteen minutes stuck is enough
    - Then email me the exact wording of the error, or bring the laptop to office hours
    - Do not spend two hours on it, and do not wait until the night before it is due

## Install 1 of 4: R

- **What it is:** the language that does the counting and the statistics
- Download it from [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org)
    - Take the newest release for your operating system and accept every default
- **On a Mac you have to pick the right file:** Apple silicon or Intel
    - Open the Apple menu, choose **About This Mac**, and read the chip line
- **Start this download now**, then keep watching, because it is the biggest of the four

## Install 2 of 4: VS Code

- **What it is:** the window you will actually work in, a free text editor from Microsoft
- Download it from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com) and accept every default
- **On a Mac**, open the downloaded file and drag **Visual Studio Code** into Applications
    - Do not run it out of the Downloads window
- Your writing, your code, and your results all live here, so you stop switching between five programs to do one thing

## Install 3 of 4: Quarto

- **What it is:** the program that turns your file into a finished document
- Download it from [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started) and accept every default
- You write prose and code in one file, press render, and get back a document with the charts and numbers already in place

## Install 4 of 4: Git

- **What it is:** the program that keeps a history of your files, so nothing you write this semester can be lost
- **Windows:** download it from [git-scm.com/downloads](https://git-scm.com/downloads)
    - The installer asks a lot of questions, and **Next** is the right answer to every one
- **Mac:** there is nothing to download
    - In Terminal, type `git --version`
    - If a box offers to install developer tools, click **Install** and wait. That box is Git arriving

## Prove All Four Are Really There

Installers fail quietly. Open VS Code, then **Terminal, New Terminal**, and run these two commands:

```bash
quarto check
git --version
```

- `quarto check` is Quarto's own self test: it checks itself, then looks for R, and prints a line for each thing it finds
- **You should see** green check marks from `quarto check` and a version number from Git
- **Windows only:** `R --version` says "not recognized" even when R is fine, because the R installer does not add R to the command line
    - On a Mac it answers normally. Either way, `quarto check` is the check that counts

## Step 1: Make Your Own Copy of the Workspace

- A **repository**, or repo, is a folder that Git is watching, and ours already has the course folder structure in it
- Go to [github.com/AURA-Lab-SIUE/v2v-workspace](https://github.com/AURA-Lab-SIUE/v2v-workspace)
- Click the green **Use this template**, then **Create a new repository**
- Name it `mc451-workspace` and leave it **Public**
- Click **Create repository**
- **You should see:** the same folders, now under your own username

## Step 2: Bring It Down to Your Laptop

- Nothing is on your computer yet. The copy exists only on GitHub
- On your new repo, click the green **Code** button and copy the URL
- In VS Code press `Ctrl+Shift+P`, or `Cmd+Shift+P` on a Mac, and a search bar drops down
- Type **Git: Clone**, press Enter, and paste the URL
- Pick a folder you will find again, such as `Documents/MC451/`
- When VS Code asks, click **Open**
- **You should see:** your folder names down the left side of VS Code

## Step 3: Let VS Code Install the Extensions

- A box appears in the bottom right: **"This workspace has extension recommendations."**
- Click **Install All**
    - That installs Quarto, R, GitLens, and the **AURA Lab R Companion**, so everyone in the course works in the same environment
- If the box already vanished, press `Ctrl+Shift+X` and search for **Quarto**, for **R** by REditorSupport, and for **AURA Lab R Companion**
- If you are stuck, the Hub page [Install VS Code](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/install-vscode.html) walks through it

## Step 4: Open the File We Wrote for You

- Download it here, or from the blue button on the [Resources page](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/index.html):
  [aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/starters/00-check-your-setup.qmd](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/starters/00-check-your-setup.qmd)
- Save it into your `mc451-workspace` folder, then open it in VS Code
- You do not have to write it, and you do not have to understand it
    - You click through it one gray box at a time, and it tells you what each box should print
- **Pause here and work through the whole file.** The rest of this video assumes you have

## What "Working" Looks Like

The file finishes by running a checker we wrote for this course:

```r
library(v2v)
setup()
```

- **You want:** green check marks all the way down **Required R packages**
- **Red next to Quarto or Git** is fine if you have not reached those steps yet
- **Red under Required** is the one that needs me
    - Email me that whole block of output exactly as it appears, rather than describing it
- Then open the Command Palette and run **Check my setup**. It runs the same checklist, and its **Install what is missing** action installs any package it flags

## When It Breaks

- **`quarto: command not found`** means that terminal opened before Quarto finished installing
    - Close it and open a new one. This is the single most common problem in the whole setup
- **`there is no package called 'v2v'`** means R is fine and the package is not there yet
    - Rerun the install step inside the check file, or run **Check my setup** and choose **Install what is missing**

## When It Still Breaks

- **Red text in R is not automatically an error.** R prints ordinary progress in red, so read the last line, not the color
- **GitHub asks for a password and refuses it.** That is not your mistake: it wants a token now
    - Click through VS Code's sign-in and it never asks again
- **Still stuck after fifteen minutes?** On github.com open your workspace repository, click **Code**, **Codespaces**, then **Create codespace on main**. R, the packages, and the Companion are already installed there

## Checkpoint

Every line should be true before you stop:

- `quarto check` comes back clean, and `git --version` answers
- Your own `mc451-workspace` exists on GitHub and is cloned into VS Code
- The extensions are installed
- `00-check-your-setup.qmd` runs and `setup()` comes back green
- **Check my setup** reports every course package installed

If any line is not true, do not leave it there. Email me the exact wording of the error, or
bring the laptop to office hours. Closing the laptop and hoping is the one approach that
never works.
